newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Phileo injects 145 mln rgt into bank unit.
newsitem.headline: Phileo injects 145 mln rgt into bank unit.

text.p: Malaysia's Phileo Allied Bhd has injected an additional 145 million ringgit in fresh equity into its wholly-owned banking unit AlliedBank Bhd to increase the bank's paid up capital to 665 million ringgit.
Executive director Lean Meng Seong said in a statement released on Saturday that the injection was a reflection of the bank's "aspiration to attain Tier-One status".

As at July 31, 1996, the bank's total shareholders' funds stood at 682 million ringgit. The figure does not include its earnings for the second half of the current financial year ending January 31, 1997.

Under Bank Negara Malaysia's two-tier banking system, a bank need to have a minimum of 820 million ringgit in shareholders' funds to attain Tier-One status which allows commercial banks to operate in more liberal conditions.

"With this enhanced financial strength, the bank is well placed to continue to grow towards being a key market player in the increasing competitive and fast liberalising financial service industry," Lean said.
